candidate.blueprint_locator: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies client-needs subcategory (13–19% of items); this item tests medication monitoring, recognition of drug-interaction risk, and interpretation of factors affecting therapeutic drug exposure.
candidate.blueprint_topic: Medication monitoring and interpretation of factors that alter antiepileptic drug exposure
candidate.educational_objective: Monitor phenytoin exposure when clinically indicated because protein binding, saturable metabolism, interacting drugs, and conditions such as hypoalbuminemia can alter clinically relevant circulating phenytoin concentrations.

options.A: Phenytoin is extensively protein bound, undergoes saturable metabolism, and has many drug interactions that can change circulating concentrations and toxicity risk
options.B: Phenytoin concentrations remain essentially unchanged by other medications, hepatic metabolism, or protein-binding changes
options.C: Serum concentration monitoring has no role when a drug interaction is suspected
options.D: In clients with hypoalbuminemia, total phenytoin concentration is always sufficient and unbound concentration never requires consideration

candidate.rationale: A is correct. Current DailyMed prescribing information for extended phenytoin sodium states that phenytoin has multiple drug interactions because of extensive plasma protein binding, saturable metabolism, and potent induction of hepatic enzymes. The label notes that inhibition of metabolism may significantly increase circulating phenytoin concentrations and toxicity risk and recommends serum-level monitoring when a drug interaction is suspected. It also directs monitoring of unbound phenytoin concentrations in patients with renal or hepatic impairment or hypoalbuminemia. B, C, and D directly contradict these labeling statements. The final item does not rely on the informal phrase 'narrow therapeutic index' when the official label provides more specific reasons for monitoring.
candidate.source_claim_supported: The current May 2026 official label directly supports clinically indicated phenytoin concentration monitoring because of protein binding, saturable metabolism, drug interactions, and altered unbound drug exposure in hypoalbuminemia or organ impairment.
